_description: ORCA (Ontology-Regularized Contrastive Alignment with Uncertainty) experiment matrix. Each ORCA experiment resolves as the base ORCA config + per-variant overrides; the generator (scripts/generate_orca_experiments.py) materializes one training_config.json per (variant x dataset x seed) under results/research_runs/, then emits a train (run_orca_training.py) + eval (run_phase1_embedding_evaluation.py) command list. ORCA runs are directly comparable to the existing OSCAR/InfoNCE baselines (E4-InfoNCE, E4-OSCAR-Skill) because they are evaluated by the identical Phase-1 embedding evaluation on the same splits/seeds. All ORCA runs require the prepared v6/v7 splits (skill_uris present) so the ontology signal is real.

trec_ct._description: TREC Clinical Trials 2021/2022. Second domain. Topic-disjoint: train+validation are 2021 topics (60/15), test is the full 2022 topic set (50). Positives are the grade-2 (eligible) pairs; graded negatives are NOT records — they live in negative_pools.jsonl and are drawn per topic by trials_domain.negative_selector.TrialsNegativeSelector. Requires base_config config/orca_trials_denominator_config.json and trials_domain.run_config.attach_trials_domain to inject the MeSH matcher and the selector.
trec_ct._why_this_dataset: The qrels are graded, and grade 1 (patient has the condition but fails eligibility) is an expert-annotated ambiguous negative — precisely the phenomenon ORCA models. Measured MeSH separation: grade1 vs grade0 Cohen's d = +0.69, so the r_ont weak target is well founded; grade2 vs grade1 d = +0.21, so the ontology is near-blind to eligibility itself and the ReliabilityMLP has real work the ontology cannot do. That combination makes the ER-NOONT / ER-NOONTW / ER-NOONTALL ablations informative here rather than degenerate, and it allows validating learned r_hat directly against the gold grade — which the career v7 split cannot support because its soft_label derives from the same ontology signals that feed r_ont.
_caveats: Anchor scarcity: 125 topics vs career v7's ~619 distinct anchors, each recurring across ~76 positives. Expect wider seed-to-seed variance than the career runs.

7 of 125 topics are diagnostic vignettes that never name the disease, so their coarse condition signal is absent and d_isco degrades to the neutral 0.5: 2021_53, 2021_67, 2022_1, 2022_10, 2022_15, 2022_17, 2022_31. The rate is worse in the test year (5/50) than the train year (2/75).

Intervention MeSH terms resolve at 81.5% (conditions: 100%): the release ships desc2021.gz but not supp2021.gz, and many drug names are Supplementary Concept Records. Adding supp2021.gz would close this.
ER-NOFUT remains untestable: TREC-CT has no repeated patient-trial interactions, so orca_use_history stays off here as on v7.

baselines.E4-InfoNCE: Pure InfoNCE, no ontology weighting, no reliability. The 'all negatives fully trusted' reference (ORCA with every reliability == 1).
baselines.E4-OSCAR-Skill: OSCAR: ontology skill-graph negatives + sample-level ontology weight. The fixed-ontology, no-reliability baseline ORCA layers on top of.

experiments.name: ORCA-Denominator (MVP)
experiments.description: Reliability folded into the InfoNCE denominator; OSCAR ontology-bucket negatives; ontology + encoder weak targets. The primary ORCA result. Its gain over E4-OSCAR-Skill is the value of learned per-negative reliability calibration.

experiments.name: ORCA-ExternalWeight
experiments.description: Reliability applied as a scalar multiplier on the final Standard_InfoNCE loss instead of inside the denominator. The HEADLINE ablation vs ER-DEN: identical reliabilities, different application site — isolates whether denominator calibration matters (Property 6).

experiments.name: ORCA-NoOntology
experiments.description: ReliabilityMLP built WITHOUT the ESCO/ISCO/OT scalar features (embeddings-only reliability), denominator calibration on. Ablation: how much of ORCA's benefit comes from the ontology features feeding the reliability estimate.

experiments.name: ORCA-NoAlign
experiments.description: Denominator calibration + adaptive negative sampling, but WITHOUT the ontology-alignment loss. Isolates the contribution of the alignment term when compared to ER-FULL.

experiments.name: ORCA-Full
experiments.description: Denominator calibration + adaptive negative sampling + ontology-alignment loss. The most ontology-retaining ORCA variant. Alignment job pairs are built in-batch from negatives carrying skill_uris.

experiments.name: ORCA-NoOntologyWeakTarget
experiments.description: Ontology removed from the weak-target SUPERVISION (orca_lambda_ont=0 -> r_tilde renormalizes to pure r_enc), while the ESCO/ISCO/OT scalars are STILL fed to the ReliabilityMLP. Identical to ER-DEN on every other factor (denominator site, adaptive sampling off, alignment off), so ER-NOONTW - ER-DEN is a clean single-factor contrast. Motivation: ER-NOONT only strips the MLP's INPUT features, but ontology still enters ORCA through r_ont = 1-exp(-beta*d_ont) in the weak targets, so the MLP can recover the ontology signal from its BCE target. This variant is what actually tests whether the ontology-derived supervision matters.

experiments.name: ORCA-NoOntologyAtAll
experiments.description: Ontology removed from BOTH sites: no ontology weak-target supervision (orca_lambda_ont=0) AND no ontology scalars in the ReliabilityMLP (orca_use_ontology_features=false). Reliability is then learned purely from warmup-encoder similarity. Also matched to ER-DEN on all other factors. This is the floor of the ontology story: if ER-NOONTALL matches ER-DEN, ORCA's gain is encoder-similarity reliability and the ontology contributes nothing; the gap ER-DEN - ER-NOONTALL is the total value of the ontology. Against ER-NOONTW it isolates the input features given no ontology supervision.

experiments.name: ORCA-ScheduleOnly (reliability neutralized)
experiments.description: THE confound control for the headline result. orca_r_min=1.0 makes clamp(r, 1.0, 1.0) == 1.0 for every negative, so the reliability-calibrated denominator reduces to Standard_InfoNCE bit-for-bit (the invariant documented on OrcaLossEngine.orca_loss); orca_eta_rel=0.0 removes the reliability BCE term so the ReliabilityMLP cannot regularize the shared projection head either. What remains is OSCAR trained under ORCA's exact 4-phase schedule (warmup -> reliability -> joint, with per-phase optimizer rebuilds). The E4-* baselines train single-phase, so ER-DEN - E4-OSCAR-Skill currently bundles reliability + schedule + auxiliary loss. If ER-SCHED lands near E4-OSCAR-Skill (~0.811) the reliability claim is clean; if it lands near ER-DEN (~0.849) the headline is really about the training procedure.

notes: ER-NOFUT (no_future / history ablation) is intentionally omitted: it is only meaningful on temporal/repeated-interaction datasets, which the v7 split is not. Add it with orca_use_history semantics once a temporal split exists.

Each run trains via run_orca_training.py (the 4-phase OrcaPhaseOrchestrator) and is evaluated by run_phase1_embedding_evaluation.py against best_checkpoint.pt, producing phase1_evaluation/phase1_evaluation_results.json — the same artifact the OSCAR/InfoNCE baselines produce.
scripts/aggregate_orca_results.py summarizes mean +/- std per variant across seeds and reports the delta vs the E4-InfoNCE and E4-OSCAR-Skill baselines.

ER-CONST (constant-reliability control) is NOT registered because it cannot be expressed config-only. Motivation: probe_reliability.py on ER-DEN s13 (2261 training pairs) found reliability confined to [0.024, 0.410], mean 0.221, within-anchor std 0.080 -- no negative is ever trusted and the UNIFORM component is ~3x the per-negative variation, so ORCA's gain may be a scale effect a retuned temperature would also buy. Why config-only fails: the clamp is clamp(r, r_min, 1.0), a LOWER bound; a model trained under a high floor still emits larger values (sigmoid reaches 1.0) and the eta_rel BCE pushes outputs toward r_tilde ~ 0.5. Verified numerically: orca_r_min=0.45 still yields clamped r in [0.459, 0.564], within-anchor std 0.025. Only orca_r_min=1.0 forces a true constant, and that is ER-SCHED (r == 1.0, no down-weighting). To implement: add an additive default-off field orca_constant_reliability (null = unchanged) that replaces the ReliabilityMLP output inside OrcaLossEngine._predict_reliability, then set it to 0.22 to match ER-DEN's observed mean with zero variance.
